Your phone recharge may cost fifteen percent more soon. Do this one thing before it does.
But first, a trick most people never notice. How many times do you recharge in a year? Twelve? Wrong.
A twenty eight day plan runs out every twenty eight days. Three sixty five divided by twenty eight is thirteen. You pay for thirteen months, every single year.

And prices may rise. Jio listed on the stock market today, twenty one percent above its IPO price. Brokers Elara and Nomura expect a twelve to fifteen percent tariff hike by March twenty twenty seven.
So how much will it cost you? Let's do the math.

The one eighty nine rupee plan, thirteen times a year, is two thousand four fifty seven. After a fifteen percent hike, about two thousand eight twenty six. That's three sixty nine extra, from one phone. A family of four? Nearly fifteen hundred a year.

The move: before the hike, recharge a longer plan. The price is locked when you pay. An annual plan costs three thousand five ninety nine today. After a fifteen percent hike, about four thousand one thirty nine. That's five forty saved on one recharge.
